[[2007]] [[Associated Press|AP All-American 1st Team]] }} '''Greg Oden''' (born [[January 22]], [[1988]], in [[Buffalo, New York]]) is an [[United States|American]] former [[college basketball]] player. He played for the [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]] [[Ohio State Buckeyes|Buckeyes]] in the 2006-07 [[NCAA]] season. He grew up in [[Terre Haute, Indiana]], playing basketball in the seventh grade at Sarah Scott Junior High School, but moved to [[Indianapolis]] in the eighth grade and attended [[Lawrence North High School]], where he led them to three straight state titles and 45 consecutive wins under coach Jack Keefer. Oden was named [[Parade (magazine)|''PARADE'']]'s High School Co-Player of the Year [[2005]] (along with [[Monta Ellis]]) and 2005 [[Gatorade]] National Boys Basketball Player of the Year, becoming the first [[high school junior|junior]] since [[LeBron James]] to be named such. Also, Oden was named [[Parade (magazine)|''PARADE'']]'s High School Player of the Year and Gatorade National Boys Basketball Player of the Year in 2006, winning the award in back-to-back years. == High school == In the 2005-06 season, Oden, a 7'0" 280 lb (2.13 m, 127 kg) senior, led Lawrence North to an undefeated record, a third straight Class 4A Indiana state championship and the first ever player to finish for an [[Indiana]] school in ''[[USA Today]]'''s Super 25 rankings. {{Fact|date=June 2007}} For the season, the [[center (basketball)|center]] scored 22.0 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 10.5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game while shooting 74 [[field goal percentage|percent from the field]]. Oden dominated in the state championship game against Muncie Central, scoring a game-high 27 points and grabbing 26 rebounds. Lawrence North won its last three state championship games by a combined 56 points and its average margin of victory during the regular season was 41 points. Oden was named 2006 Mr Basketball in Indiana. He was also on the McDonald's All-American Team and played in the All-American game. == College == On [[June 29]], [[2005]], Oden and Lawrence North teammate as well as best friend [[Mike Conley, Jr.|Mike Conley]] announced that they would be attending [[Ohio State University]] starting with the 2006-07 season. Oden had surgery on his right wrist on [[June 16]], [[2006]], in Indianapolis to repair a ligament injury late in his senior high school season. As a result, he sat out the beginning of the 2006-07 season with Ohio State, during which his team was ranked as high as first before losing to [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. He made his college debut on [[December 2]], 2006, against [[Valparaiso Crusaders basketball|Valparaiso]], coming off the bench. He finished the game with 14 points, 10 rebounds and 5 blocks. As of [[March 14]], [[2007]], Oden has averaged 15.5 points, 9.7 rebounds, and 3.5 blocks per game.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=31545 Greg Oden's ESPN profile] The Big Ten honored Oden with ''Player of the Week'', along with [[Wisconsin Badgers|Wisconsin]]'s [[Alando Tucker]], on [[January 29]], [[2007]]. In the previous week he had averaged 18 points and 11.5 rebounds.{{cite news | title = Oden Earns First Big Ten Weekly Award | publisher = Ohio State University Department of Athletics | date = [[2007-01-29]] | url = http://ohiostatebuckeyes.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/012907aaa.html | accessdate = 2007-01-29 }} On March 6, 2007, Oden was named First Team All-[[Big Ten]] as well being voted the conference's Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite news | title = Oden to named First Team All-Big Ten, Defensive Player of the Year | url = http://bigten.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030607aad.html}} Oden fouled out for the first time in his college career against Xavier in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, and was bothered by foul trouble throughout the tournament. In the [[Sweet Sixteen (NCAA Basketball Tournament)|Sweet Sixteen]], Oden blocked a potential game-winning shot in the final seconds against Tennessee to preserve an 85-84 victory, and went on to lead Ohio State past Memphis and Georgetown to advance to the 2007 National Championship. In the title game, Oden scored 25 points, 12 rebounds, and had 4 blocked shots in a losing effort against the [[Florida Gators basketball|Florida Gators]]. On [[March 26]], [[2007]], Oden, along with [[Kevin Durant]], [[Arron Afflalo]], [[Alando Tucker]], and [[Acie Law IV]], was named to the Associated Press All-American Team. Oden and Durant are the first freshmen voted to the All-American First Team since 1990 and the third and fourth overall. NBA analyst [[Steve Kerr]] has described Oden as a "once-in-a-decade player."{{cite news | last = Kerr | first = Steve | authorlink = Steve Kerr | title = Questions and The Answer | publisher = [[Yahoo! Sports]] | date = [[2006-12-15]] | url = http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=sk-mailbag121506&prov=yhoo&type=lgns | accessdate = 2007-01-29 }} On May 23, 2007, Oden was added to the current roster for the [[United States men's national basketball team]]. ==NBA career== ===Pre-draft (2007)=== On [[April 20]], [[2007]], Oden announced that he would be entering the NBA Draft. Former [[UCLA]] center and [[Basketball Hall of Fame|NBA Hall of Famer]] [[Bill Walton]] said that the world hasn't seen more than flashes of what Oden can do on offense. http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=214148 On [[May 23]], Oden flew to [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] to meet with [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] executives to talk about a shoe contract.{{cite news |url=http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/18842394/ |title=Oden flies to Portland . . . to talk sneakers |date=2007-05-24 |publisher=MSNBC.com |accessdate=2007-05-29}} On [[May 29]], Oden signed with [[Topps]] Trading Card Company to a 3-year deal worth at least $3 million. His first deal is a card featuring Oden and [[Bill Russell]]. [http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2886171] On [[June 19]], Oden flew to Portland to meet with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and went through a workout and physical examination on June 20.
